entries.english:
CCLXXXIV. Emperor Charles IV enfeoffs the bishop and chapter of Breslau with the town of Grottkau and its associated district. From the original in the cathedral chapter archive, DD. 37. The familiar large imperial seal of white wax, with its counterseal, hangs from yellow and green silk cords.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen. Charles IV, by divine favor ever august Roman Emperor and King of Bohemia, makes known to all by these present letters, for perpetual remembrance, that the late Boleslaus, former Duke of Silesia and Lord of Brieg, during his lifetime held in fief from the late King John of Bohemia, our dearest father, the town of Grottkau with its land, district, fortifications, and all its boundaries, borders, extent, rights, and appurtenances; [the transcription breaks off here].

[Editorial notes: 1) The emperor’s monogram appears here. 2) For the recognition, see document no. CCLXXXI. 3) Printed in Lünig, *Spicilegium ecclesiasticum*, continuation II, p. 1104. The surviving witness list names the highest master of our chamber, Jodocus and Johannes, brothers of Rosenberg, Sdenco of Sternberg, judge of the royal court in Bohemia, and many other of our princes, nobles, and faithful men. Given at Breslau in the year of the Lord 1358, in the eleventh indiction, on the Ides of December, the thirteenth year of our reign and the fourth of our empire.]
